feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform expertise. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scope indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and broad tool stack.  
- Writing is concise and professional, with a strong focus on digital strategy, governance, operations, and cross-channel leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scale: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, production savings, engagement gains, process efficiency, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper value proposition would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your niche: digital strategy and communications leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more specific strengths tied to outcomes: platform modernization, editorial systems, cross-channel operations.
- Shorten the final sentence to emphasize advocacy/policy translation and stakeholder alignment.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the editorial workflows and systems that enable complex teams to operate effectively. Strong in advocacy and policy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, operational, and production capabilities, but several items are broad or repetitive with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership themes will make this section sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and standardize style: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Replace generic items with more distinctive strengths: “CMS modernization & administration” and “Content operations & editorial workflow design.”
- Prioritize senior-level capabilities first: digital strategy, platform modernization, analytics, governance, stakeholder alignment.
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Platform modernization & CMS administration • Multi-channel communications • Content operations & editorial workflow design • Data analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow systems & governance • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Multi-channel communications,” and “Policy & advocacy communications” closely repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial systems and governance” and technical workflow content elsewhere.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and AI/search leadership.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, enterprise web modernization, and content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign/microsite frameworks, modular content components, and downloadable toolkit experiences.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points, e.g. governance/workflows/analytics in one bullet; CMS/front-end/troubleshooting in another.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow efficiencies, search improvements, stakeholder groups served, or engagement/performance lifts.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects “AI Hybrid Search”; keep one high-level here and save technical detail for Projects.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consultant-specific contributions and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add % improvements, time/cost savings, engagement growth, reporting adoption, or production savings for the studio and analytics work.
- Consolidate channel language: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials” rather than listing platforms broadly.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize building the in-house studio and scaling capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more outcome-focused and position it as the bridge between hands-on production and later digital leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with progression + ownership: “Promoted to lead NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; launched/scaled weekly advocacy video update; coordinated cross-team editorial calendar; standardized publishing workflows.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” with direct verbs: “scaled,” “standardized,” “coordinated,” “established.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; emphasize that this role expanded it into a recurring channel.
- “Publishing workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version tactical, not governance-heavy.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder engagement
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder engagement” or “Mission-driven communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning styles.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve proof points like “10,000+ page migration” or “50+ publishers” for experience bullets, not skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep this skills item high-level and differentiated.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI-enabled search; move WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages later or drop 1–2.
- Tighten wording: change “Airtable systems” to “Airtable-based operational systems” and “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue aligned to recent work, e.g., “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed platform/tool inventory in “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and executive-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Keep only the most decision-relevant tools here; move the full stack to Technical + IT. Suggested version: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten wording and add leadership emphasis: “Executive dashboarding” is stronger than “Leadership reporting”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — KPI framework design, executive dashboarding, SEO/performance analysis, and insight generation using GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”
- Avoid repeating every tool here if they already appear in the Technical + IT section

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and event delivery rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more distinctive phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “Video production leadership” to align with the studio build in recent roles.
- Combine related items for concision: merge “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” into one stronger line.
- If space allows, add a scale cue tied to recent work, e.g. “supporting advocacy programming and recurring event coverage.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; vary wording here to avoid repetition.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ systems may be better kept only if you want hands-on production emphasized; otherwise it can feel too tactical for a senior profile.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: **CMS platforms for enterprise web modernization, campaign microsites and content operations**
- Consider trimming lower-signal tools if not used meaningfully in recent roles; **GitHub Pages** may read as lightweight beside enterprise platforms
- Alternative rewrite: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places
- Drupal is already heavily evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this item should complement that evidence, not restate it

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tooling rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more senior-facing list: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless tooling: Cloudflare Workers • Deployment/automation: GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV is targeting hands-on developer roles; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner.
- Consider replacing “Coding & Technical Implementation” with “Technical Implementation & Integrations” to better match your recent work.
- If true, add one short qualifier tied to impact elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “supporting Drupal builds, campaign microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; keep the fuller detail in one place only.
- “API integrations” and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and “Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize categories and strongest tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop Basecamp unless it was used recently or materially; it feels older/less relevant than the others.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with your recent leadership work.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect tools to outcomes instead of listing only platforms, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate supporting editorial planning, approvals, and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams overlap with general collaboration rather than technical depth; keep only if this section is meant to include operational tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and underplays your stronger, recent leadership in email operations. It should signal enterprise-scale platform ownership rather than just list products.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and tighten naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parenthetical form: **Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications), Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation), Mailchimp (smaller-scale campaigns)**
- If space allows, connect to impact instead of tools only: **Platforms supporting newsletters and advocacy communications reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here if that metric already appears prominently under Director/Associate Director roles.
- “Multi-channel communications” is already covered elsewhere; keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, add scale or output metrics to show early impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split broad claims into concrete actions: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate’s daily production work.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated in later roles; here, specify what changed operationally.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the standout achievement. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize the podcast launch and innovation/program support without repeating higher-level communications language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest impact: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination, program support, and digital storytelling.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague terms like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific outcome or format if possible (e.g., web features, multimedia briefs, member resources).
- If available, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, or programs/projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on firsts and foundational work.
- Avoid “oversaw” here if later entries already show leadership at a larger scale.
